examples: An agent stops on a permission dialog while your mobile device is locked: the installed app pushes "approval needed" straight from your computer to Apple, and tapping it opens the app.
A push does not arrive: settings shows the last result for that device, for example 403 from the push service, so the cause is visible.
Your phone gets permission and question pushes only, while your tablet gets nothing: untick the tablet's column.
how_to: Open the installed app (added to the home screen), go to settings, notifications, alerts on this device, and press alerts on. Allow notifications when asked.
Press send test to push one "approval needed" to every subscribed device now; remove drops a device.
Routes: GET /api/v1/push/vapid-public-key, POST and GET /api/v1/push/subscriptions, DELETE /api/v1/push/subscriptions/{id}, POST /api/v1/push/test.

Each subscribed device is its own column in the routing matrix (settings, notifications, routing): tick the notification types that device should get. A new device starts with the global default ticks.
Pushes for the same type to the same device within 10 seconds are coalesced into one.
media_exempt: A permission prompt and a system notification: neither is capturable from the app's own page.
name: Web push alerts
summary: a push from this computer to your mobile device or browser, with a fixed typed title and body per notification type, so no session name or question text leaves the computer beyond what that type's copy says.
where: Settings, notifications, alerts on this device (the button shows only in the installed app). The worker is /sw.js.
